Texas WebCoders sets one up for Houston, TX businesses from $149/month plus a $299 one-time setup, and most go live in 7 to 14 days. Houston is the largest city in Texas, and its size, heat, storms and bilingual customers put heavy pressure on every business phone line.

Why Houston businesses miss calls

Houston covers a huge area, from the Ship Channel to the Texas Medical Center and the Energy Corridor. Construction employs about 10% of workers and professional services over 16%. Traffic alone can keep a service crew out of reach for hours, and August heat or a Gulf storm can bring a wave of urgent calls. Several AI receptionist providers already serve Houston, so compare voice quality and support carefully.

Which Houston businesses benefit most?

  • HVAC and contractors: Summer heat makes AC calls urgent, and crews lose hours to traffic.
  • Medical offices: Clinics can answer routine calls in English or Spanish.
  • Law firms: Injury and immigration callers often phone the first firm that answers.

What a call could sound like in Houston

Here is an example of how a call might go. Your script, rules and wording would be set up with you.

Caller: Se descompuso el aire y hace mucho calor. ¿Pueden venir hoy?

AI receptionist: Replies in Spanish, marks it urgent and sends the job to your on-call tech.

Does your Houston AI receptionist need Spanish?

About 37.7% of Houston residents age 5 and older speak Spanish at home. About 38% of residents speak Spanish at home, so a bilingual agent is a practical need for most Houston businesses. Our AI calling agents and AI receptionists speak English and Spanish, and you can read more on our bilingual AI calling agent page.

Can you keep your Houston phone number?

Yes. Houston callers will usually see the 281, 346, 713 and 832 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
